# Spine 0.7.5 API guide

> Assemble once in BuildApplication, declare input sources, use public context views, and verify real behavior.

This guide targets Spine core v0.7.5 and CLI v0.4.4. Check /en/community/versions for published tags and compatible platform versions. CLI installation and app dependency channels are independent. Use Go 1.26 or later for the examples, and honor the selected modules' go directives. Preserve source, go.mod and go.sum.

## Create and verify

```sh
go install github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-cli/cmd/spine@latest
spine version
spine new my-app --module example.com/my-app --channel main --validator playground --no-interactive
cd my-app
spine doctor
spine inspect
spine contract check
spine verify
spine dev
```

The default layout is layered-v1. BuildApplication lives in internal/application/application.go and returns (spine.App, boot.Options, error). Generated main assembles, validates and runs. --validator playground creates playground.New() in BuildApplication and registers spine.WithValidator(engine). The default validator none does not check validate tags. There is no boot option that automatically calls arbitrary DTO Validate methods.

contract check analyzes static contracts. verify adds formatting, vet and Go tests. Neither proves real HTTP, DB or broker behavior. app.Validate does not execute constructors. Prepare executes DI and route collection without starting listeners or consumer loops; initialization can still touch external resources. Run manages preparation, serving and shutdown. Arbitrary DI Close methods are not automatically called.

## Constructors and routes

Implement Constructor(dependencies...) *Self and register constructor.Repository, Service, Controller, Interceptor, or Custom. Marker fields are not copied. Factories support one return value, not (T, error) or variadic parameters. Ordinary []T parameters are supported. Instances are shared within the app; never overwrite singleton fields with request transactions.

Controllers implement RegisterRoutes(*api.Registry). Pass an inline handler to r.GET(path, func(...) { ... }, options...) and use r.Group(prefix, options...) for related routes. A group "/" route refers to its base. api.Interceptors((*Auth)(nil)) resolves a registered interceptor through DI. Group policies are inherited; route policies append. Registration of an interceptor role does not itself apply a scope.

## Public context

HTTP handlers can declare github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/spine.Ctx at any parameter position when they need the request context. All interceptor hooks receive this type, commonly imported as spinectx alongside the root app package. Standard context.Context injection into handlers remains compatible.

- ctx.ExecutionContext().Set/Get shares values within one execution.
- ctx.ExecutionContext().Context() supplies standard context to services, repositories and publish.Event.
- ctx.HTTPRequestContext() and HTTPResponseContext() return a view plus a support boolean.
- ctx.WebSocket() returns the WebSocket view for handshake and message request information.
- Check the boolean before using a transport view. Consumer executions do not have HTTP views.
- Views do not expose internal Bind, SetRoute, writer replacement, EventBus or SenderKey.
- Do not retain request contexts after completion. Stores are released after completion hooks; later Get returns no value and Set does nothing.

## HTTP inputs and DTO validation

Use input.Path[T] for a scalar or DTO, input.Query[T], input.Header[T] and input.Body[T] for DTOs. input.Param does not exist. Bare *DTO HTTP inputs fail with HTTP_INPUT_WRAPPER_REQUIRED.

Path, Query and Header default to lowerCamel names: ID -> id and UserID -> userId. Override with path:"id", query:"name" or header:"X-Request-ID". Body follows JSON/XML/form decoder naming. Read body.Name or path.ID directly and dereference scalar inputs. A path DTO may bind a subset of keys; scalar inputs must match route variable count and order. Do not mix scalar and DTO Path styles.

One handler accepts at most one Body. JSON, XML, URL-encoded form and multipart are supported. Use form-tagged *multipart.FileHeader or []*multipart.FileHeader fields for files; temporary files are cleaned after completion. Malformed or conflicting XML tags fail preparation.

A validator registered with WithValidator checks validate tags after binding and before the handler. Failures return HTTP 400. If tags suffice, do not add a DTO Validate method or duplicate checks in handlers. A custom method is an ordinary Go method called explicitly as (*body).Validate() or (*CreateUser)(body).Validate(). The wrapper does not expose body.Validate(). OpenAPI does not infer custom method bodies.

## Errors and lifecycle

Return one httpx.Response[T], httpx.Binary or httpx.Redirect, optionally with error. Multiple response values fail preparation. HTTPError accepts only 400–599; 200/302 errors and ordinary errors become sanitized 500 responses. Only deliberately public messages belong in httperr.

Both global and route PreHandle hooks run before input binding. Global HTTP hooks run before routing with empty HandlerMeta. Route hooks receive selected metadata. BeforeResponse runs in reverse only after successful PreHandle and sees binding, execution and response-preparation errors. Its error takes response priority over a handler error; the last failing BeforeResponse wins. Previous errors remain available to AfterCompletion.

AfterCompletion runs after the response write attempt and may be called even when PreHandle was not reached. Check resources exist. Commit/rollback belongs in BeforeResponse, not AfterCompletion. Pass request bun.Tx explicitly as bun.IDB to services and repositories. DB commit, event publishing and response delivery are not one atomic transaction; use an outbox when needed.

## OpenAPI and message transports

Enable boot.HTTPOptions.OpenAPI explicitly, and register Swagger UI or ReDoc if needed. playground supplies SchemaDescriber alongside runtime validation. Without a describing validator, do not expect full input models. OpenAPI does not execute validation. Required metadata comes from the validator, including when json:",string" limits other constraints. Custom methods and handler-selected statuses are not inferred.

New controller routes are collected during Prepare. Use spine.DescribePreparedHTTP on the prepared app and close it when finished. spine.NetHTTPHandler(prepared) returns (http.Handler, error) where supported. OpenAPI JSON/UI/assets bypass business interceptors; protect their publication through HTTP middleware or a proxy. CLI static export does not run the validator; inspect its diagnostics and the runtime schema.

WebSocket message DTOs are plain structs, not HTTP Body wrappers. Send with ws.Send(ctx.ExecutionContext().Context(), ws.TextMessage, payload). This has three arguments and addresses the current connection. Do not obtain senders from internal context keys. Event consumers also use plain message DTOs; publish with publish.Event(ctx.ExecutionContext().Context(), event).

## Deprecated compatibility

Keep existing app.Route, route.WithInterceptors, query.Values, header.Values, query.Pagination, legacy path wrappers and multipart.UploadedFiles only for compatibility. New scaffold and example code must use current APIs. Do not mix deprecated HTTP inputs with new Path/Query/Header wrappers in one handler. ctx.Get is deprecated; use ctx.ExecutionContext().Get. Application code must not import spine/internal packages.

If your app uses the retracted Go module version v0.7.1, see /en/learn/migration/v0.7.5#from-v071.

## Complete DI example

Install the documented 0.7.5-compatible core and Echo versions, save as main.go and request /greeting.

```go
package main

import (
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine"
	echoplatform "github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-echo-platform"
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/api"
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/boot"
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/constructor"
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/httpx"
	"log"
)

type Repository struct{}

func (*Repository) Constructor() *Repository { return &Repository{} }
func (*Repository) Greeting() string         { return "hello" }

type Service struct{ repository *Repository }

func (*Service) Constructor(repository *Repository) *Service { return &Service{repository: repository} }

type Controller struct{ service *Service }

func (*Controller) Constructor(service *Service) *Controller { return &Controller{service: service} }
func (c *Controller) RegisterRoutes(r *api.Registry) {
	r.GET("/greeting", func() httpx.Response[string] {
		return httpx.Response[string]{Body: c.service.repository.Greeting()}
	})
}
func BuildApplication() (spine.App, boot.Options, error) {

	app := spine.New(echoplatform.Option())
	app.Constructor(constructor.Controller(&Controller{}), constructor.Service(&Service{}), constructor.Repository(&Repository{}))
	return app, boot.Options{Address: ":8080", HTTP: &boot.HTTPOptions{}, EnableGracefulShutdown: true}, nil
}
func main() {
	app, options, err := BuildApplication()
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := app.Validate(options); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := app.Run(options); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```
